::: section-card
## **Methodological moderators**

This section presents methodological moderators that may influence estimates of mixed-paternity prevalence across studies. We focus on marker type, nest-box use, nest type, and study duration, because these variables can affect both the detection and reporting of mixed paternity. All models use the same multilevel phylogenetic beta-binomial structure as the overall model.
:::

Model-based prevalence is summarised as the posterior mean on the probability scale, with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals. The inverse-logit transformation is applied to each posterior draw before averaging; all random effects are set to zero.

## Model

This helper function documents the shared model structure used for all single-moderator models. These models are fitted outside this website workflow and saved as `.rds` files.

The marker-type model uses 0 + marker_type_model, with one logit coefficient per marker category and no shared population-level intercept. Nest-box use and study duration retain an intercept. Model-specific reference categories and priors are documented in the [overall-model chapter](03_overall_model.qmd#model-coding-and-priors).

```{r}

#| eval: false
#| echo: true

fit_single_moderator <- function(formula, data) {
  brm(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    family = beta_binomial(link = "logit"),
    data2 = list(phylo_mat = phylo_mat),
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 10000,
    warmup = 5000,
    control = list(
      adapt_delta = 0.99,
      max_treedepth = 15
    ),
    seed = 123
  )
}
```

## Marker type

This model tested whether estimated mixed-paternity prevalence differed among molecular marker types.

### Figure

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Figures/Figuresmarker_type.png")
```

### Model summary

```{r}

#| #| message: false
#| #| warning: false
#| #| code-fold: true
model_marker_type_0 <- readRDS("models/model_marker_type_0.rds")
summary(model_marker_type_0)
```

### Prevalence table

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

marker_type_probability_draws <- 100 * plogis(brms::fixef(model_marker_type_0, summary = FALSE))
marker_type_prevalence <- data.frame(
  `Marker type` = sub("^marker_type_model", "", colnames(marker_type_probability_draws)),
  `Posterior mean prevalence (%)` = colMeans(marker_type_probability_draws),
  `Lower 95% CrI` = apply(marker_type_probability_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  `Upper 95% CrI` = apply(marker_type_probability_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(marker_type_prevalence, digits = 2)
```

### Post-hoc comparisons

Pairwise contrasts are posterior means with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals. Each contrast compares the first category with the second. Log-odds differences are calculated within each posterior draw. Odds ratios are summarised after exponentiating each difference, so mean OR is the mean of the transformed draws, not the exponential of the mean log-odds difference.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

b <- brms::fixef(model_marker_type_0, summary = FALSE)
pairs <- combn(colnames(b), 2L, simplify = FALSE)
marker_type_contrasts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(pair) {
  difference <- b[, pair[1L]] - b[, pair[2L]]
  odds_ratio <- exp(difference)
  data.frame(
    contrast = paste(sub("marker_type_model", "", pair, fixed = TRUE), collapse = " - "),
    estimate = mean(difference),
    lower.CrI = unname(quantile(difference, 0.025)),
    upper.CrI = unname(quantile(difference, 0.975)),
    OR = mean(odds_ratio),
    lower.OR = unname(quantile(odds_ratio, 0.025)),
    upper.OR = unname(quantile(odds_ratio, 0.975))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(marker_type_contrasts, digits = 3,
  caption = "Posterior means and 95% equal-tailed intervals: log-odds contrasts and odds ratios.")
```

## Study duration

Study duration was included as a methodological moderator because longer studies may provide more stable estimates of mixed-paternity prevalence and may differ from short-term studies in sampling intensity and temporal coverage. It was standardised using all 607 non-missing records in the 619-record overall analytical dataset (mean = 3.649 years, SD = 3.452 years).

### Figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-study-duration-common-scaling
#| fig-cap: "Population-level predicted mixed-paternity prevalence across study duration from the refitted single-moderator model. Study duration was standardised using the overall analytical dataset; points show observed record-level prevalence and the ribbon shows the 95% credible interval."
#| echo: false

knitr::include_graphics("Figures/common_scaling/study_duration.png")
```

### Model summary

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show fitted-model summary"

cat(readLines("logs/common_scaling/model_study_duration_summary.txt"), sep = "\n")
```

###  Model estimates

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

study_duration_table <- readr::read_csv(
  "tables/common_scaling/model_study_duration_fixed_effects.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  dplyr::filter(term == "study_duration_sc") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Parameter = "Study duration (per 1 SD = 3.452 years)",
    Estimate,
    `Lower 95% CrI` = Q2.5,
    `Upper 95% CrI` = Q97.5
  )

knitr::kable(study_duration_table, digits = 3)
```

Longer studies were associated with lower mixed-paternity prevalence on the log-odds scale ($\beta$ = -0.088, 95% CrI -0.167 to -0.009).

## Nest box

Nest-box use was included as a methodological moderator because studies conducted in nest-box populations may differ from studies of natural nests in monitoring accessibility, sampling completeness, and opportunities for detecting mixed paternity. This variable may also capture biological differences associated with nesting-site availability, breeding density, and local neighbourhood structure.

The intercept represents the reference category - natural nests .

### Figure

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Figures/Figuresnest_box.png")
```

### Model summary

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true

model_nest_box <- readRDS("models/model_nest_box.rds")
summary(model_nest_box)
```

###  Model estimates

```{r}
#| label: nest-box-effect-table
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

s_nest_box <- summary(model_nest_box)

nest_box_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Parameter = rownames(s_nest_box$fixed),
  Estimate = s_nest_box$fixed[, "Estimate"],
  `Lower 95% CrI` = s_nest_box$fixed[, "l-95% CI"],
  `Upper 95% CrI` = s_nest_box$fixed[, "u-95% CI"]
)

knitr::kable(nest_box_table, digits = 3)
```

The nest-box association was positive but uncertain: posterior mean beta = 0.285 (95% equal-tailed CrI −0.062 to 0.632), and posterior mean OR = 1.351 (0.940 to 1.882). The OR mean is calculated as mean(exp(beta_draws)), whereas exp(mean(beta_draws)) = 1.330. The difference is due to nonlinear averaging (Jensen’s inequality), not rounding. Both intervals include their respective null values.

```{r}
#| label: nest-box-or-scale-check
#| code-fold: true
beta_draws <- brms::fixef(model_nest_box, summary = FALSE)[, "nest_box_modelyes"]
scale_check <- data.frame(
  beta_mean = mean(beta_draws),
  exp_beta_mean = exp(mean(beta_draws)),
  OR_mean = mean(exp(beta_draws))
)
knitr::kable(scale_check, digits = 6)
```

## Heterogeneity summary

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
variance_table <- readr::read_csv("tables/variance_audit/group_level_variances.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(Model %in% c("Overall model", "Marker type", "Nest box", "Study duration"))
knitr::kable(variance_table, digits = 3)
```

Group-level entries are posterior mean variances on the logit scale, calculated by squaring each posterior SD draw before averaging. Phi is the beta-binomial precision parameter. Models use different complete-case samples; these tables do not measure heterogeneity explained by individual moderators.
